newsitem.title: USA: Mazda sees flat '97 U.S. vehicle sales.
newsitem.headline: Mazda sees flat '97 U.S. vehicle sales.

text.p: A top Mazda Motor of America Inc executive said Thursday the company's 1997 U.S. vehicle sales and market share are expected to be flat with 1996 figures.

George McCabe, general manager of the unit, the North American arm of Mazda Motor Corp, said the production ramp-up of new vehicles such as the 1998 626 midsized sedan will hold back efforts to boost unit volume and market share.
Mazda sold about 238,000 vehicles in the U.S. in 1996 for a 1.6 percent share of the market. McCabe and other Mazda officials appeared at the New York International Auto Show.

In addition to the 626, Mazda took the wraps off its new 1998 B-Series compact pickup truck, and a concept version of its Protege sedan tailored for women. The new products are aimed at revitalizing the Mazda nameplate, which has been suffering from tepid sales at a time when other Japanese automakers are experiencing booming U.S. growth.

The 626 was designed exclusively for the North American market. The car is longer and wider on the outside for a smoother ride and features a stiffer body for more rigidity. Interior room has also been increased, as well as trunk volume. The engine comes in two versions, a 2.0-liter four cylinder and a 2.5-liter V-6. Mazda has made a radio and CD player standard on all LX and ES models.

Production of the cars will start at Mazda's Auto Alliance joint venture in Flat Rock, Mich., in July, and take about six months to get up to full production. McCabe said annual production is slated at 85,000 units.
Mazda plans annual production of 50,000 to 60,000 of the B-Series pickups. The truck is based on the Ranger from Ford Motor Co with a different body and interior features.
Pricing has not been set for either vehicle. They will go on sale in October.
